grades.quote: FENCE instructions executed in U- mode are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O implies also the requirement to order main memory accesses
grades.reason: Covers only the modified U-mode interpretation of the FENCE PI/PO/SI/SO bits when senvcfg.FIOM=1. It shows what the predecessor and successor bits mean in that special case. It does not give the base meaning of the fields.

grades.quote: FENCE instructions executed when V=1 are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O implies also the requirement to order main memory accesses
grades.reason: Covers only the modified interpretation of the FENCE PI/PO/SI/SO bits when henvcfg.FIOM=1 and V=1. It is auxiliary to the question and does not give the base meaning of the predecessor and successor fields. The rest of the passage covers unrelated henvcfg fields.

grades.quote: The other RV32I HINTs are encoded as FENCE instructions with a null predecessor or successor set and with _fm_ =0.
grades.reason: Mentions FENCE encodings with a null predecessor or successor set as HINTs. It does not explain what the predecessor and successor fields select. It only gives the incidental point that a null set imposes no ordering.

grades.quote: Any combination of device input (I), device output (O), memory reads (R), and memory writes (W) may be ordered with respect to any combination of the same.
grades.reason: Directly explains that the predecessor and successor sets select any combination of device input, device output, memory reads and memory writes. It also explains the ordering semantics: operations in the successor set are not observed before operations in the predecessor set.
